label: Exploratory: same method as the presets, not checked against a national reference series.

mask_rule.rule: A cell-year is too_few_fires when the fixed-clock (expected) Aqua count is under 300, or the 95% interval half-width is over 25% of L, or L or its interval is not a finite number. The first two are the preset audit's own insufficient_data rule (analysis/statistics/audit.py).
mask_rule.applies_to: status is the 2025 reading, status_2024 the 2024 reading. A masked reading carries no L, interval or outside_noise value.
mask_rule.meaning: too_few_fires means the count is too small to read. It does not mean the count agreed with the fixed clock.

benchmarks.name: Presets reproduce look times from grid cells
benchmarks.check: median Aqua local solar time of near-nadir detections in each preset's cells (the G1 cell sets), 84 preset-years 2012 to 2025, against data/out/drift/*.json
benchmarks.result: 84 of 84 within 5 min; largest 2.4 min; largest difference in the 2024 or 2025 shift 2.0 min
benchmarks.tolerance_basis: The drift files are rounded to the minute (0.5 min). A sun-synchronous look time changes by about 0.5 to 0.7 min per degree of latitude, and a 2-degree cell set can move the fire-weighted latitude of a preset by a few degrees, so a few minutes of offset is geometry, not error. The quantity being mapped moved 40 to 80 min, so 5 min keeps the check meaningful. Set before the comparison was run.

auditor.notes: ASSUMPTIONS: (1) Aqua = rows with satellite=='Aqua' exactly in the modis zips; S-NPP = rows with satellite=='N' exactly in the viirs-snpp zips; daytime = daynight=='D' exactly; no other filter. (2) rows_read = every data row (header excluded) of every CSV member of the 14 modis zips and the 14 viirs-snpp zips, before any satellite/daynight filter (so modis includes Terra and night rows). (3) Every row is counted as it appears; rows are NOT de-duplicated across country files. (4) Days are assigned by the acq_date string; day 0 = 2012-01-01; month/year are the calendar month/year of acq_date; block = day // 16. (5) Cell edges: lon0 <= longitude < lon0+2 and lat0 <= latitude < lat0+2 on the float values as parsed. (6) Retained-day test uses whole-archive daytime counts of the same row sets as in (1). (7) Counts on non-retained days are set to zero everywhere (baseline, target, bootstrap). (8) aqua_count and snpp_count are over retained days of the target year. (9) Bootstrap: w = default_rng(20261114).poisson(1.0,(1000,320)) as the first draw; replicate L recomputed from weighted counts incl. the Vb[m]>0 fallback; non-finite L dropped; numpy.percentile linear. (10) Rounding with Python round() on the float64 result; JSON numbers drop trailing zeros, so e.g. 0.98 means 0.980 and 1.06 means 1.060. (11) Files for other years and viirs-jpss1 were not opened; the non-CSV readme member in each zip was skipped. context.note: Context for reading the map. Exploratory; none of this is checked against a national reference series.

placebo_control.what: For cells with an ok 2025 reading: how often one 2012-2020 year, scored against the other eight, falls outside the range of the other eight's scores. Exchangeable years would give about 2 in 9 (0.22). Compare with share_outside_placebo_range above.

whole_earth.what: One series for all listed cells together, scored as one area (its own month ratios). Not the sum of the cell readings.

retained_days_sensitivity.what: The layer keeps a day when both satellites returned a daytime detection anywhere on Earth. A partial outage that removes some orbits still passes that rule. Here the rule is applied per 30-degree longitude band (close to the preset audit's 'anywhere in Brazil'), and the two sets of cell readings are compared. cells_all.csv carries both.
